The Hadith then proceeds to cite the prohibition of consuming drinks fermented in pumpkin shells, hollowed wood and dyed containers. [^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Teaches the Injunctions of Deen While Travelling for the Farewell Hajj

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that after living in Madinah for nine years, Rasulullaah ﷺ did not perform Hajj until the announcement was made one day that Rasulullaah ﷺ would be performing Hajj that year. A great multitude of people then arrived in Madinah with the intention of following Rasulullaah ﷺ and doing what he did. There were still five days left of Dhul Qa'dah when Rasulullaah ﷺ left (Madinah) with the Sahabah (RA). It was when they reached Dhul Hulayfah that Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abu Bakr (RA) was born to Hadhrat Asmaa bint Umays (RA). She sent a message to ask Rasulullaah ﷺ what she was to do, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied saying, "Take a bath, use a cloth to hold the blood and enter into Ihraam."
Rasulullaah ﷺ then proceeded further and it was when his camel took him to Baydaa that he called out the Talbiya of Towheed saying:

blocks.arabic_text: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ

blocks.text: The Sahabah (RA) also recited the Talbiya and although Rasulullaah ﷺ heard some of them add phrases like " " ("Dhal Ma'aarij"), he did not rebuke them. Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "The people in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ reached as far as I could see. They were on foot and on animals. Behind Rasulullaah ﷺ were just as many people, and there were also that many on his right and his left. Rasulullaah ﷺ was in our midst and he was well aware of the meanings of the Qur'aanic verses that came to him. We therefore did exactly what we saw Rasulullaah ﷺ doing." [^2]

The aspects of Deen that Rasulullaah ﷺ taught the Sahabah (RA) on this journey and in the sermons he delivered during the Hajj will be quoted in the chapter discussing Hajj. Some of it has however passed in the chapter discussing learning while out in Jihaad.
